openQuestions: Bun's module resolution auto-installs any missing import on the fly (from its global cache ~/.bun/install/cache or over the network) whenever it finds NO node_modules anywhere upward from cwd (default --install=auto, https://bun.com/docs/runtime/auto-install). This means test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts's zero-third-party-dependency guard, even after this story's fix (rooting in the real OS tmpdir instead of the repo-local scratch root), is reliable only in a network-sandboxed CI runner (nothing to auto-install) -- NOT on a developer machine with network egress or a matching stale global-cache entry, where a genuine third-party import added to the vendored script could silently auto-install and pass. Measured live 2026-08-06 (see scripts/cam/patterns.md bullet, US-R1-001). Not fixed in this story: the review finding this story addresses was specifically about the repo-local scratch root deterministically resolving cam-cli's own node_modules, which is now fixed; this Bun-auto-install nuance is a separate, preexisting characteristic of the test's design (true since before this PRD), not introduced by GOTCHA 10(a) or by this story's fix. Flagging for a future story/issue if a stronger guard (e.g. spawning with an explicit --install=fallback-disabling flag, or asserting via strace-style import tracing) is wanted.

scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts and scripts/check-debt-markers.ts share the identical substring-match EXCLUDED_DIRS bug this story fixed in scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts (p.includes('vendor/') wrongly swallows the legitimate test/vendor/ subdirectory, so those two sibling gates have never actually scanned test/vendor/**). Left unfixed: this story's file-scope is check-test-tmpdir.ts only (the gate whose ALLOWLIST this story populates); the sibling gates were not touched by the story's own diff. Worth a small follow-up story if those gates' coverage of test/vendor/ matters.
nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 fixed the CRITICAL review finding at test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts:29 (GOTCHA 10(a)): the US-007 migration had re-rooted this test onto the shared repo-local scratch root (.cam-test-tmp/, createTestTmpdir), which lives inside the cam-cli checkout, so the test's own premise (a directory with NO resolvable node_modules, mirroring the vendored smoke script's zero-third-party-dependency invariant) was silently defeated -- Node-style module resolution walked up and deterministically found cam-cli's own node_modules (containing js-yaml). Fix: this ONE file now roots directly in the real OS temp dir (mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cam-smoke-standalone-')), node:os/node:fs imports restored, createTestTmpdir import removed), with a new ALLOWLIST entry in scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts (the mechanism US-008 built specifically for this kind of justified exception) documenting why. This is ALLOWLIST's first real (non-empty) entry. Populating it surfaced two more things that needed fixing to make the story correct, not just the headline swap: (1) filterScannablePaths in scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts had a pre-existing bug -- EXCLUDED_DIRS matched 'vendor/' etc. as a bare substring, which wrongly swallowed the legitimate test/vendor/ subdirectory (a real test dir, not an embedded vendor copy), meaning test/vendor/** was never actually scanned by this gate since it shipped in US-008; fixed by splitting into TOP_LEVEL_EXCLUDED_DIRS (now startsWith-matched, since the glob is always rooted at test/ so these can only ever matter for the CLI's optional custom scanRoot arg) and NESTED_EXCLUDED_MARKERS (still substring-matched, for .cam-test-tmp, which legitimately needs catching at any depth) -- pinned by a new filterScannablePaths test. (2) every scanForTmpdirRoots(...) unit-test fixture that didn't pass an explicit allowlist arg relied on the function's default parameter (= ALLOWLIST); once ALLOWLIST held a real entry outside those synthetic single-file file-sets, findStaleAllowlistEntries correctly-but-spuriously flagged it as stale, adding a phantom extra finding to 8 previously-passing tests -- fixed by passing an explicit [] second argument to every fixture test that isn't itself exercising the allowlist mechanism, and updating the 'the real ALLOWLIST export stays empty' test to assert the new single-entry shape instead. scripts/file-size-budget.json's ceiling for the standalone test file was raised 86->95 (measured via content.split('\n').length, not wc -l) with a dated _ref note prepended and staged before re-running the gate, per the CLAUDE.md rubric. bun run typecheck clean; bun test 6067 pass / 0 fail (one net new pinning test vs. the prior 6066); bun run check:all fully green (file-size, coverage, debt-markers, dead-code, dup, lint, embed-vendor, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, test-tmpdir, skip-ratchet all ok) after the file-size raise landed. A SEPARATE latent bug was DISCOVERED but deliberately NOT fixed here (documented in openQuestions and scripts/cam/patterns.md instead, per Surgical Changes): Bun's own module resolution auto-installs any missing import on the fly whenever no node_modules exists anywhere upward from cwd (default --install=auto), so even this story's real-OS-tmpdir fix does not fully guarantee the zero-dependency invariant on a developer machine with network egress or a stale global-cache hit -- only in a network-sandboxed CI runner is the guard fully reliable. scripts/cam/prd.json in the working tree already carried an unrelated pre-staged diff at session start (three new US-R1-00x review-follow-up stories inserted plus renumbered priority fields on the existing US-001..US-009 stories) that this session did not author; it was included in this commit only because 'commit ALL changes' is the standing instruction and the diff was already present before this story began -- the next agent should treat scripts/cam/prd.json as reflecting whatever the supervisor/reviewer most recently wrote, not something this story's own diff changed the meaning of. Next agent should check prd.json for the next non-passing, non-operator story (likely US-R1-002, the exit-time-reaper-never-fires-under-bun-test CRITICAL finding at test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts:90, priority 2) before assuming more work is needed.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Fetched to validate the fix's premise (a real OS tmpdir root with no node_modules upward guarantees module resolution fails for a third-party import). Docs confirm the opposite: Bun's default --install=auto abandons Node-style resolution and AUTO-INSTALLS any missing import from its global cache or the network whenever no node_modules is found upward, so the guarantee only holds deterministically for the specific failure mode this story fixes (repo-local scratch root resolving cam-cli's OWN already-installed node_modules), not universally. Live-measured corroboration (mktemp -d + `import yaml from 'js-yaml'` still auto-installed from ~/.bun/install/cache and crashed on an unrelated ESM shape mismatch) recorded in scripts/cam/patterns.md and handoff.openQuestions rather than acted on further, since it is a preexisting characteristic outside this story's specific review finding.
